content.title: Oklahoma starts postseason play against Colorado in College Basketball Crown first round
content.text: LAS VEGAS -The Oklahoma Sooners men’s basketball begin postseason play Wednesday night, facing Colorado Buffaloes men’s basketball in the opening round of the College Basketball Crown.Tipoff is set for 7 p.m. CT inside the MGM Grand Garden Arena, with a potential $300,000 NIL prize awaiting the tournament champion. Prize money, opportunity fuel excitement The unique tournament format — and financial incentive — has players energized heading into the matchup.“I’m excited, man. I mean, I get to hang out with the guys. We get to go to Las Vegas. I mean, we get to play,” said Nijel Pack. “I’m going to definitely cherish every moment… whether it’s dinnertime with the guys, whether it’s on the floor.”Head coach Porter Moser said the stakes have not gone unnoticed.“Our guys are excited, just the format of the whole… let’s just say, yeah, the prize money,” Moser said. Sooners enter hot Oklahoma comes into the tournament with momentum, winning eight of its last 11 games, including six of its last seven.The Sooners were one of the last teams left out of the NCAA Tournament but made a strong push in the SEC Tournament, going 2-1 with wins over South Carolina and Texas A&M before falling to Arkansas.During that stretch, OU shot 49% from the field and averaged fewer than eight turnovers per game. 3-point shooting key for OU Perimeter shooting has been a strength all season.The Sooners led the SEC in conference play with a 39% mark from 3-point range and are shooting 42% from deep over their last 10 games.Leading the way is Pack, one of the top shooters in the country.The veteran guard ranks among active Division I leaders in both career points and 3-pointers, shooting 45.2% from beyond the arc this season. What’s next With a win, Oklahoma would advance to Saturday’s semifinals to face either Baylor or Minnesota.The opposite side of the bracket includes Creighton, Rutgers, Stanford and West Virginia.Three wins would secure the tournament title — and the $300,000 prize.
